summary: The recorded base reproduced the same-ID pending-load removal bug. At the exact candidate commit, removal is explicitly rejected with success=false while the load remains pending, satisfying one of the original issue's allowed lifecycle contracts. Candidate regression tests, independent adversarial boundaries, and the existing NGRAM corpus suite passed.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction against the actual base implementation. The same-corpus removal during a synchronized pending load returned success=True; the other two boundary tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-fc2c549eb929/base_candidate_regression.log
Candidate regression: same-ID pending removal rejected, different-ID removal allowed, and post-commit same-ID removal allowed. 3 passed. Raw output: reports/j-fc2c549eb929/candidate_own_tests.log

Independent cases: finished-but-unpolled load remains protected, failed pending load is not falsely reported removed, and a different corpus remains removable. 3 passed. Raw output: reports/j-fc2c549eb929/candidate_independent.log
Existing NGRAM corpus and HTTP mock coverage. 42 passed. Raw output: reports/j-fc2c549eb929/candidate_existing_ngram.log
Candidate patch hygiene. Only archived candidate log files contain trailing whitespace; no functional source issue was reported. Raw output: reports/j-fc2c549eb929/candidate_diff_check.log

gpu_execution_evidence: The bug is a Python scheduler/control-plane state transition and was reproduced with deterministic thread synchronization. The prepared single AMD Instinct MI350X was identified, but no unrelated GPU smoke was used as fix evidence.
remaining_limitations: The exact Qwen3-4B serving reproduction was not run because the model weights were not provided.
The prepared system is one AMD Instinct MI350X with ROCm 7.2, not the reporter's NVIDIA L40S/CUDA architecture.
No end-to-end HTTP server was launched; direct testing exercised the actual ExternalCorpusManager implementation that owns the reported transition.
The candidate's archived log artifacts contain trailing whitespace, causing git diff --check to return nonzero; this does not affect runtime behavior.
